author: a. j. zhao
title: Hawai'i softball falls to UC Santa Barbara in series opener - Maui Reporter
text:
The University of Hawai’i softball team lost 4-0 to UC Santa Barbara in their series opener on April 3, ending the Rainbow Wahine’s five-game conference win streak. Despite getting at least one runner on base in all but two innings, Hawai’i left eight runners stranded during the game at Campus Diamond in Santa Barbara.
The loss marks a setback for Hawai’i, which now holds a 16-16 overall record and an 8-5 mark in Big West play. The game highlighted challenges for the Rainbow Wahine offense as they struggled to capitalize on scoring opportunities against UCSB’s defense.
Hawai’i managed five hits and three walks throughout the contest. Their best chance came in the fourth inning when Millie Fidge led off with a single and was joined on base by Nagasako after two outs, putting both runners in scoring position. However, UCSB responded with a strikeout looking to end the threat.
UC Santa Barbara built its lead through extra-base hits. Delaina Ma’ae hit solo home runs in both the third and sixth innings. In between, Ainsley Waddell doubled and scored on Emily Carr’s double down the left-field line in the fourth inning. Dani Rauscher also contributed by scoring after Giselle Mejia’s ground-rule double to center field.
Taryn Irimata pitched a complete game for Hawai’i but took her seventh loss of the season after allowing four runs on nine hits with three strikeouts over 91 pitches. UCSB pitcher Sophia Clark earned her eighth win with a complete game shutout, surrendering five hits while striking out three batters and walking three.
The teams are scheduled to conclude their three-game series with a doubleheader on April 4 at Campus Diamond.
